force_encoding: float32 little-endian, config-major; per config the flat C-order sequence of the OpenMM (N,3) force array (x1,y1,z1,x2,...), i.e. Julia reshape(flat,3,N)

perturbation.applies_to: all three components for every config >= 1; amplitude 0.02*config nm
perturbation.index_base: i is 0-based; d is the Cartesian component (0=x, 1=y, 2=z); config = 1,2,...
perturbation.note: config 0 is unperturbed. config 1 uses amplitude 0.02 nm, config 2 uses 0.04 nm, etc., in double precision. No coordinates are stored.

source.force_field: AMBER ff14SB protein + OpenForceField-parameterized catechol ligand (residue UNL) from PDB 1XEP; the solute-only prmtop/coordinates are derived from the MIT-licensed ljmartin/mmpbsa_from_openmm preparation at commit 48664084b88e7cf4f731e5ab4082a7edd8198345 (openmm_simulation/complex_plus_water.parm7 + openmm_simulation/complex_coords.pdb, solute-only, no box, NoCutoff reference)
source.attribution_note: An earlier version of this file attributed the preparation to the third-party amber_tutorials tutorial repository. That attribution was wrong (that repository holds an IL2 + SP4206 system, not the 1XEP T4 lysozyme + catechol system) and is explicitly rejected: the owner, commit and evidence are recorded in chemistry/fixtures/protein_ligand/PROVENANCE.json, key 'attribution_correction'. The accepted source is ljmartin/mmpbsa_from_openmm at commit 48664084b88e7cf4f731e5ab4082a7edd8198345.
